To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have discovered a new type of gene expression pattern, latent global expression (LGE), and have developed an automated system that uses this new type of pattern to perform classification and clustering of gene expression patterns, as well as image retrieval.
1. We have developed an automatic system, FEMine, which can be used for gene expression image classification, clustering, or image retrieval.

we present a new system for automatic mining of fruit fly gene expression images, which uses automatically discovered latent spatial themes of gene expressions, and that our experiments show that our system outperforms existing systems for gene expression analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods and tools for automatic analysis of gene expression patterns.

the development of methods for automated gene expression analysis in the Drosophila melanogaster embryo, which can be used to identify and characterize gene expression patterns, to cluster genes according to their expression patterns, and to retrieve images according to their gene expression content.
the development of novel methods and systems for image-based gene analysis, and their application to the study of gene expression in fruit flies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FEMine is a powerful tool to analyze and explore the spatial expression patterns of genes in the Drosophila embryo.
the FEMine system is an important step forward in the field of image-based gene expression data analysis.
our method is the first to automatically discover and exploit latent spatial gene expression themes in a collection of whole-embryo images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FEMine is a fully automatic, high-throughput system for image-based Drosophila gene expression analysis.

we have developed a system that can automatically analyze the whole-embryos in an image collection, and extract latent spatial patterns of gene expressions that can be used in various downstream applications.
FEMine is a novel and effective method for image-based gene analysis, and that the LGEs are an important and useful concept for gene expression image analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of spatial context in the analysis of gene expression data can be very effective in the absence of any prior knowledge about gene function.
the use of LGEs, discovered automatically by our FEMine, leads to a more robust and effective image mining system than previous methods.
the latent themes discovered by FEMine are more robust to the variability in gene expression than previously proposed methods.
